title: The $A$-optimal design problem and the $S$-matrix conjecture
summary: The $S$-matrix conjecture was formulated by Sloane and Harwit in 1976, motivated by an $A$-optimal design problem arising in spectroscopy. It states that if $A$ is a nonsingular real $n\times n$ matrix whose entries lie in $[0,1]$, then $$\left\|A^{-1}\right\|_F\ge\frac{2n}{n+1}.$$ Moreover, equality holds if and only if $A$ is an $S$-matrix. In this paper, we prove the conjecture by combining a variational trace inequality in odd dimensions with a sharp range-constrained estimate for the Moore--Penrose inverse of a centered matrix in even dimensions.
